# Radoslav Radev Recommends Pressing The Legs Together For Planche And Opening The Legs More For Straddle Planche

Radoslav Radev recommends pressing the legs together for planche progressions to increase strength, and for straddle planche to think about opening the legs more to lift them automatically. [src: vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 01:55]

## Details

- Pressing the legs together can be applied to almost every single progression. [src: vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 01:53]
- When the legs are relaxed, all focus is on the upper body and you are not thinking about the lower body. [src: vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 02:11]
- When you are on tuck, pressing the legs together, tuck, advanced tuck. [src: vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 02:22]
- A lot of people have weak full planche because they do not press their legs together. [src: vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 02:27]
- On straddle planche, instead of thinking to lift the legs, try to open them maximum as you can and you lift them automatically. [src: vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 02:59]

## Evidence

- vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 01:53 (Radoslav Radev): "Almost every single progression, you can apply this rule."
- vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 01:55 (Radoslav Radev): "And this rule is to press the legs together."
- vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 02:11 (Radoslav Radev): "So all of your focus is on the upper body, but you're not thinking for the lower body and actually you're lifting your lower body."
- vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 02:22 (Radoslav Radev): "When you are on tuck, pressing the legs together, tuck, advanced tuck."
- vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 02:27 (Radoslav Radev): "By the way, when you're on full planche, a lot of you guys, you have weak full planche because you don't press your legs together."
- vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 02:59 (Radoslav Radev): "If you want to lift your legs, don't think just to lift them. Try to open them maximum as you can and you're lifting them automatically."
- vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 03:05 (Radoslav Radev): "I realized it after a lot of years and nobody told me."

## Why This Matters

He says he realized this rule after a lot of years and nobody told him about it. [src: vid-9U5LctaDyY0 @ 03:05]
